title: SDK quickpath toolchain manifesto & labs
content:
Overview
This is a working manifesto for a compact SDK quickpath and accompanying toolchain codelabs aimed at drastically reducing time-to-first-success for new internal teams and external adopters. Focus is on a single linear journey that scales: 3-minute token check, 15-minute hello world, 60-minute production smell test.

Objective
- Shrink first happy path to < 15 minutes for an engineer who knows HTTP.
- Provide a single reproducible repo that contains: tiny sample app, smoke tests, telemetry probes, and production checklist.
- Remove local environment friction by shipping a hermetic sandbox and opt-in remote demo mode.

Principles (short)
- Minimal surface area: start with the simplest request type (text generation) and extend.
- Observable from day one: builtin telemetry and a tiny dashboard for latency/cost per token.
- Fail loudly, recover gracefully: clear error messages and an explicit fallback flow.
- Portable tooling: same steps work against hosted API, dedicated, and private.

Target personas
- Product engineers integrating a single endpoint.
- Platform engineers evaluating rollout/telemetry.
- Solutions engineers running proofs for customers.

Problem statement
Current onboarding is fragmented: a cookbook here, a long README there, sample apps in multiple repos. New adopters hit 3 classes of friction: env setup, auth/key management, and understanding cost/latency tradeoffs. We unify these into a single quickpath developer loop.

Quickpath flows (proposed)
1) 3-minute smoke
   - Goal: confirm credential and endpoint.
   - Steps: install tiny CLI (one script), run 'quickpath check', see green/red.
2) 15-minute hello world
   - Goal: make a simple generation and render response in minimal UI (static HTML).
   - Steps: clone sample, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, run dev server, press generate.
3) 60-minute production smell test
   - Goal: instrument sample to show token-level metrics, autoscaling hint, and a canary rollback policy.
   - Steps: enable telemetry in sample, run load script, review dashboard.

Compact codelabs (v1 layout)
- lab-1-quickcheck: credential, region, simple health check script.
- lab-2-hello-gen: tiny polyglot sample (node + python) with minimal UI, a few prompts.
- lab-3-telemetry-and-cost: integrate client-side probes and server aggregation, show cost per request.
- lab-4-failover-flow: simulate model capacity decline and demonstrate fallback to cheaper variant.
Each lab is 10-20 steps, includes expected artifacts and a one-command verifier.

Toolchain components
- tiny-cli: bootstrap env, run smoke tests, collect telemetry snapshot.
- hermetic-sandbox: docker compose for local dev with a stubbed response service and a local trace collector.
- sample-apps: node-express and flask minimal examples with JS UI.
- verifier: script produces a short human-readable report with pass/fail and next steps.
- docs: a single README that maps to the 3 flows and points to advanced topics.

Telemetry & success metrics
- Must capture: request latency p50/p95, tokens in/out, model name, region, API key age.
- Success criteria: 70% of new signups complete hello world in <= 15 minutes in user testing.
- Developer feedback loop: short in-lab survey link captured at the end of lab-2.

Acceptance criteria for v1 quickstart
- One-click repo clone and setup script with <= 6 manual inputs.
- Sample app runs locally without cloud dependencies (uses sandbox).
- Telemetry shows a live trace for each sample request.
- Smoke verifier returns exit code 0 for happy path.
- Clear failure messages and documented remediation steps.

Checklist: deliverables for v1 (owners in parens)
- tiny-cli script and installer (Rohit)
- hermetic-sandbox compose + stub service (Marco)
- node + python minimal samples and UI (Lina)
- lightweight telemetry collector example and dashboard seed (Ava)
- README and 3 lab markdowns (Ava + Lina)
- smoke verifier script + CI job (Rohit)
- UX copy for error messages and onboarding checklist (PM review)

Open questions
- Which authentication patterns do we show by default: API key only, or API key + short-lived tokens?
- Do we include a managed demo mode that uses a public demo key, or ask devs to sign up?
- Quantization and performance knobs: show or hide in v1?

Minimal smoke test (example)
- Quick manual command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model": "redwood-small", "input": "hello"}' | head -c 200
- In docs we provide the exact curl and also show how the tiny-cli wraps that in 'quickpath check'. Note: escape sequences in sample are intentionally simple for readability.

Next steps & owners
- Week 1: prototype tiny-cli and hermetic-sandbox, validate local flow with 3 engineers (Rohit + Marco)
- Week 2: ship node sample and hello-gen lab, run 3 user tests (Lina + Ava)
- Week 3: telemetry hook + dashboard seed, add verifier CI job (Ava + Rohit)
- Week 4: polish UX copy and open beta to SEs, gather metrics

Appendix: short user testing script
- Task 1: run quickpath check and note time to completion.
- Task 2: follow lab-2, make a successful generation, answer quick survey.
- Task 3: optional - run load generator and look at latency chart.

Notes to self
- Keep labs modular so we can reuse lab-2 content in a separate "enterprise" kit that includes private deployment toggles.
- Aim for one canonical sample repo, not multiple forks.

Action items (today)
- Create repo skeleton and add LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING, and one-line README (Ava)
- Draft tiny-cli minimal interface spec: commands quickpath check, lab run, verifier (Rohit)
- Wire up sandbox stub to return deterministic latency and token counts (Marco)
